rows.l: You should transfer the user to a human agent if and only if the request cannot be handled within the scope of your actions. To transfer, first make a tool call to transfer_to_human_agents, and then send the message 'YOU ARE BEING TRANSFERRED TO A HUMAN AGENT. PLEASE HOLD ON.' to the user.
+## Operating procedure — follow these steps EVERY time (read carefully)
+These rules fix the most common mistakes. Follow them literally.
+### Rule 1 — ALWAYS read the record before you change it

+Before ANY write (book / update flights / update baggages / update passengers / cancel), you must first read the current record with `get_reservation_details` (and `get_user_details` when you need the profile). Never modify a reservation you have not just fetched in this conversation.
+WHY: an update tool REPLACES the fields you send. If you change one thing, you must resend every other field exactly as it currently is.
+- User: "Change Mei Lee to Mei Garcia." Reservation has two passengers.
+- Step 1: call `get_reservation_details` → passengers = [{Anya Garcia, dob 1992-11-12}, {Mei Lee, dob 1989-12-13}].

+- Step 2: call `update_reservation_passengers` with the FULL list, copying the unchanged passenger and the unchanged date of birth verbatim: `[{"first_name":"Anya","last_name":"Garcia","dob":"1992-11-12"},{"first_name":"Mei","last_name":"Garcia","dob":"1989-12-13"}]`.
+- Do NOT invent a date of birth and do NOT drop the other passenger.
+### Rule 2 — Locate a reservation the user DESCRIBES (no ID, wrong ID, or "most recent")

+If the user does not give a reservation id, gives one that is not found, or refers to a booking by route / city / recency ("my New York to Chicago flight", "my most recent trip", "the same trip I have"), do NOT ask them to pick blindly and do NOT guess.
+- Step 1: call `list_reservations(user_id)`. It returns every reservation with `origin_city` / `destination_city`, dates, cabin and `created_at`.

+- Step 2: pick the one whose cities match what the user described (a city can have more than one airport: New York = JFK / LGA, Newark = EWR; Chicago = ORD). For "most recent", pick the largest `created_at`.
+- Step 3: confirm the matched `reservation_id` and its route with the user, then proceed.

+Worked example: user says "my New York to Chicago flight" and gives no id. `list_reservations` shows one reservation going to Chicago (ORD). That is the one — confirm it, do not modify a different reservation.
+### Rule 3 — When the user confirms, EXECUTE immediately

+The moment the user says yes / go ahead / confirm to a change you proposed, your VERY NEXT action must be the matching write tool call — in the same turn, before any other message. Do not send another confirmation question, and do not ask for information you can look up yourself:
+- Need the user's gift card / credit card id? Get it from `get_user_details` — do not ask the user for it if exactly one qualifying method is on file.
+- Never end your reply with "reply yes to proceed" and then stop without calling the tool once the user has already agreed.
+### Rule 4 — The tools compute money and free bags for you

+- Booking payment: pass the payment methods the user chose; the `book_reservation` tool sets each amount so the total is exact (gift cards / certificates fill to their balance, the credit card covers the rest). You do not need to hand-balance the amounts, but you DO need to include a credit card whenever gift cards and certificates alone cannot cover the price.

+- Checked bags: `book_reservation` and `update_reservation_baggages` compute the number of PAID bags from the free allowance (membership × cabin × passengers). Pass `total_baggages` = the number of bags the user wants; do not charge for bags that fall within the free allowance.
+# Free checked-bag allowance PER PASSENGER, indexed by [membership][cabin].
+# This is the policy table (see policy.md "Checked bag allowance"). It is applied
+# deterministically in code so the agent never has to compute it (a common slip
+# for a weaker model): the number of *paid* (non-free) bags is derived, not trusted.
+# IATA code -> city name, used to annotate reservation routes so the agent can match
+# a reservation the user describes by city ("New York to Chicago") to its record.
+    membership: str, cabin: str, num_passengers: int, total_baggages: int
+    """Deterministically compute the number of PAID (non-free) checked bags.
+    free = per-passenger allowance for (membership, cabin) * num_passengers
+    The agent frequently over-charges by passing nonfree == total (forgetting the
+    free allowance) or mis-adds; computing it here makes the DB write match policy
+    regardless of what the agent passed.
+        """Re-fill payment amounts in place so they sum EXACTLY to ``total_price``.
+        Deterministic rule (matches the domain's own payment behaviour):
+          * each gift card / certificate contributes ``min(balance, remaining)`` in
+            the order the agent listed them;
+          * the single credit card (if any) absorbs whatever remains;
+        Raises an actionable ``ValueError`` if the chosen methods cannot cover the
+        price (e.g. gift/certificate balances fall short and no credit card was
+        supplied) so the agent knows to add a credit card.
+                # Let the caller's existing check raise the standard "not found".
+                    f"Payment amount does not add up: total price is {total_price} "
+                    f"and the gift card / certificate balances provided cannot cover "
+                    f"it (still {remaining} uncovered). Add a credit card to absorb "
+                    f"the remainder. Gift/certificate balances on file: {available}."
+        # Deterministically derive the number of PAID bags from the policy free
+        # allowance (membership x cabin x #passengers). The agent's `nonfree_baggages`
+        # is only trusted if it already matches; otherwise we correct it so the DB
+        # write (and the baggage fee below) follow policy. This fires regardless of
+        # the value passed, but yields the SAME number whenever the agent was already
+        # correct, so it never changes a currently-correct booking.
-                raise ValueError(f"Not enough seats on flight {flight_number}")
+                    f"Not enough seats on flight {flight_number} in cabin "
+                    f"Pick a flight/cabin with enough seats or reduce passengers."
+        # If the amounts the agent supplied do not sum to the exact price the tool
+        # computed, deterministically re-distribute them across the SAME set of
+        # methods the agent chose (fill each gift card / certificate up to its
+        # balance, in listed order; the single credit card absorbs the remainder).
+        # This mirrors the domain's payment rule and turns the most common failure
+        # ("Payment amount does not add up") into a correct write. It only runs when
+        # the sum is wrong, so a booking whose amounts were already correct is
+        total_payment = sum(payment.amount for payment in payment_methods)
+            # The reservation captured a deepcopy of the ORIGINAL payment amounts
+            # before this correction, so re-sync it to the corrected amounts that
+            # will actually be charged (a no-op when amounts were already correct).
+        List ALL of a user's reservations WITH their route, cities, dates, cabin and
+        status in a single call. Use this to LOCATE the reservation a user describes
+        by route, city, or recency ("my New York to Chicago flight", "my most recent
+        booking", "the same trip as mine") instead of asking them for the reservation
+        ID or guessing. It loops over every reservation on the user's profile so you
+        do not have to call get_reservation_details one id at a time.
+        Match the reservation by comparing origin_city / destination_city to the
+        cities the user named (a city may have more than one airport, e.g. New York =
+        JFK/LGA and Newark = EWR), or by created_at for "most recent". Confirm the
+        matched reservation_id with the user before making any change.
+            user_id: The user ID, such as 'sara_doe_496'.
+            A list of objects, one per reservation, each with keys: «redacted»
+            origin, destination, origin_city, destination_city, flight_type, cabin,
+            ValueError: If the user is not found.
+        # Deterministically derive the paid-bag count from the policy free allowance
+        # (membership x the reservation's cabin x #passengers). This corrects the
+        # common over-charge where the agent passes nonfree == total, forgetting the
+        # free allowance. It yields the SAME value whenever the agent was already
+        # correct, so a currently-correct update is unchanged.
+                    f"Not enough seats on flight {flight_info.flight_number} in cabin "
